questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Very interesting location. Fellow EU-member, also i wanted to study the language

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Erasmus has way too much paper work and makes it a chore to do something that is otherwise interesting. (One example making we write this report again because the session times out)

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Generally pretty easy. And if something was unclear then the coordinators at the faculty were quick to help

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Faculty coordinators

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Three student dorms at different pricepoints

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The dorms have shared kitchens, but you can go to student restaurants and get a full meal for under 2 Euros

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Very small, i would recommend staying and Cvjetno or Radić dorms, as the rooms are bigger

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Generally easy. Sometimes info can be missing on the courses, but by communicating with the university will quickly give you the answers

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Mostly online by using Email. Then there is one mandatory introduction day

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Coordinators who are quick to help and can be reached by Email, phone or by showing up at the faculty

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100% succesful everbody at the university are very helpful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Better to write one Email too many than not write.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I attended the language course at Croaticum, which is very good, but also intensive, with class and homework every day.
My other courses were without classes and require you to be able to work independently, but it makes it way more flexible.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Way closer to my experience at high-school when it came to Croaticum, but this is most likely because it works the best for learning a language.
The other courses were without classes, so mostly online communication and the option to come in for consultations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Croaticum B1/B2
Sociology:
- Terrorism and society
- International and national security
- Sociology of business decision making

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Croaticum is very good if you want to learn the language, but beware of the workload.
My other courses were also good as they allowed me to be more flexible with my time.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to pay for enrollment at the university (around 50 Euros).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out and café/bars are cheap. But grocery shopping is similar to Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Trips to: Museums, Parks, Exhibitions.
various social events and parties.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the ESN events (especially the intro week programme)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go outside of Zagreb to the rest of the country and places like Slovenia, Budapest, Bosnia.
Flixbus is your best friend

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, people are friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and social, they will quickly open up to you and become good friends

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not so much the university students, but a lot of local people are way more conservative compared to the average Dane

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The "go with the flow" relaxed attitude to most things

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be social
2. Go outside Zagreb
3. Meet locals

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go to as many events as possible

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Academically: Balancing paperwork and focusing on studies.
Personally: Making a lot of very good friendships and spending almost every day with them for months, but then suddenly having to leave and to say goodbye

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Try too keep in contact with the people you meet during your stay.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
